hot.title: Claude Opus 5 System Card
hot.summary: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 demonstrates substantial advancements in large language model capabilities across diverse domains, including setting new state-of-the-art on benchmarks like SWE-bench Pro (79.2%) and ARC-AGI-3 (30.16%). Extensive pre-deployment evaluations confirm its high harmless response rates (e.g., 98.54% on claude.ai) and classify it as Anthropic's most aligned model to date, while conservatively identifying CB-1 level chemical/biological capabilities but not CB-2.

hot.title: Open Weights and American AI Leadership
hot.summary: A coalition of technology companies and foundations asserts that open-weight AI models are vital for American AI leadership, arguing they promote a diffuse, competitive, and secure AI ecosystem. This approach is claimed to enable widespread innovation, reduce costs across diverse sectors, empower users with greater control, and enhance AI safety through transparency and community-driven remediation.

hot.title: Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding (HOPE): A Mathematical Framework for Deconstructing Learned Representations in Deep Networks
hot.summary: Introducing the Hilbert Operator for Progressive Encoding (HOPE), a mathematical framework that models deep network neurons as rank-1 Hilbert-Schmidt operators in a continuous Hilbert space, enabling unbiased and data-free (for BN networks) deconstruction of learned representations. This framework facilitated superior structured model compression and a novel transfer learning method, DEFT, which balanced stability and plasticity more effectively than baselines by analytically partitioning core and slack neurons.

hot.title: Expanding Flow Maps
hot.summary: This research introduces Expanding Generative Flows (EFlows) and their distilled counterpart, Expanding Flow Maps (EFMs), which overcome the fixed-dimensionality limitation of current generative models by enabling dynamic expansion of the state space during inference. The framework successfully generates high-quality, variable-sized outputs across continuous molecular conformer generation, discrete molecular graph generation, and variable-length language modeling, often achieving competitive or superior results with fewer sampling steps.

hot.title: AREX: Towards a Recursively Self-Improving Agent for Deep Research
hot.summary: The AREX agent, developed by BAAI, introduces a recursively self-improving framework for deep research that leverages the asymmetry between discovering and verifying answers. It incorporates an autonomous context updating mechanism to manage information across long research horizons and uses specialized training techniques, consistently outperforming comparable-scale baselines and competing with frontier models on a diverse set of benchmarks.

hot.title: Visual Contrastive Self-Distillation
hot.summary: Visual Contrastive Self-Distillation (VCSD) introduces a method for vision-language models to create a self-distillation signal by contrasting predictions under original and content-erased visual conditions. This approach consistently improved aggregate accuracy across seven benchmarks by up to 4.77% for Qwen3-VL 2B and 4.27% for Qwen3.5 9B models, without requiring external teachers or privileged information.

hot.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
hot.summary: OPENFORGE RL is an open-source framework enabling end-to-end training of advanced AI agents directly within their complex deployment harnesses and environments, addressing the train-deploy mismatch in large language models and vision-language models. The framework demonstrates performance improvements over existing baselines in both text-based tool-use and multimodal GUI tasks.

hot.title: Skill Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of LLM Capability with Co-Evolving Skills
hot.summary: Researchers from Alibaba and affiliated universities introduce Skill Self-Play (Skill-SP), a reinforcement learning framework that enables Large Language Models to autonomously improve by co-evolving a task proposer, a solver, and a dynamic library of modular skills. The framework consistently enhanced the performance of five diverse LLM backbones on complex tool-calling and logical reasoning benchmarks, demonstrating its ability to generate high-quality, verifiable curricula and significantly improve initially misaligned models.

hot.title: Project Pilot: Can AI control a drone?
Context-weighted Discrete Flow Matching
hot.summary: Researchers from the University of Amsterdam and Meta FAIR introduced Context-weighted Discrete Flow Matching (DFM), an approach that integrates local context into the generative dynamics for improved discrete sequence modeling. This method enhances text generation quality, reducing perplexity by 63% on OpenWebText, and boosts molecular generation, increasing valid molecules by 2.8x on QM9 compared to standard DFM.

hot.title: SANA-Video 2.0: Hybrid Linear Attention with Attention Residuals for Efficient Video Generation
hot.summary: NVIDIA's SANA-Video 2.0, a video Diffusion Transformer, efficiently generates high-quality video by integrating a hybrid linear attention mechanism with periodic softmax anchors and attention residuals. The 5B model generated an 81-frame video in 13.2 seconds on a single H100 GPU, achieving a VBench Total score of 84.30 while offering a 3.2x faster DiT forward pass for 720p/60s compared to full-softmax baselines.

hot.title: SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction
hot.summary: SM4RT introduces a Structure-of-Motion (SoM) representation for 4D dynamic scene understanding, decomposing scene dynamics into physically grounded 6D twists (motion bases) and per-pixel assignments. This framework achieves strong performance in 3D reconstruction and tracking from monocular RGB video, while enhancing physical coherence and interpretability of object movements.

hot.title: Twins: Learn to Predict Unified Representations with Focal Loss
hot.summary: The Twins framework introduces a unified continuous visual token space by concatenating semantic-rich ViT features and detail-preserving VAE latents, resolving the "impossible triangle" trade-off between understanding, reconstruction, and generation. Its training leverages a novel Focal Loss for Flow Matching to mitigate optimization imbalance, enabling state-of-the-art image reconstruction with 31.46 PSNR, competitive multimodal understanding, and high-quality image generation with a 1.59 gFID on ImageNet@256.

Towards Trustworthy and Cost-Efficient Data Integration: From Naïve RAG to Agentic RAG
hot.summary: Ma and Khan propose a conceptual framework for "Agentic RAG" to enhance trustworthiness and cost-efficiency in LLM-based data integration. It evolves from naive RAG by incorporating adaptive retrieval, iterative multi-agent reasoning, batch processing, and graph-based memory, addressing limitations of existing approaches like hallucination and high computational costs.

hot.title: Scaling Native Multimodal Pre-Training From Scratch
hot.summary: Researchers at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and Tencent systematically characterize the scaling properties of native multimodal pre-training from scratch, revealing distinct compute-optimal allocation behaviors for language and multimodal objectives. Their findings provide quantitative guidance for efficiently scaling unified multimodal models, showing that a higher multimodal data ratio necessitates a shift towards increased data scaling over parameter expansion.

hot.title: dRAE: Representation Autoencoder with Hyper-Spherical Codes
hot.summary: The dRAE (discrete Representation Autoencoder) framework, developed by researchers from the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences and Ant Group, introduces Hyper-Spherical Quantization (HSQ) to effectively discretize high-dimensional visual features. This approach overcomes codebook collapse, allowing for scalable vocabulary sizes and demonstrating improved performance in image reconstruction, multimodal understanding, and visual generation tasks.

hot.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Structured Dynamics from Videos
hot.summary: Researchers from Fundamental AI Lab, UTN, and University of Oxford introduce a Structured Dynamics Model (SDM) that recovers disentangled camera and object motion representations from frozen pretrained image features. This model, trained with weak self-supervision, achieves performance competitive with strongly supervised 3D models on various motion understanding tasks and improves action recognition by 9.6 percentage points over a prior self-supervised approach.

likes.title: Masked Visual Actions for Unified World Modeling
likes.summary: Researchers from Stanford University and collaborators developed Masked Visual Actions (MVA), a pixel-space control interface that enables a single pre-trained video model to function as a unified world model for both forward and inverse dynamics in robot manipulation. This approach achieved superior visual fidelity and cross-embodiment generalization in controllable video generation, improved planning success rates by up to 26% on Robocasa tasks, and demonstrated zero-shot inverse modeling with 90% success on a complex pick-and-place task.

likes.title: LLM-as-a-Coach: Experiential Learning for Non-Verifiable Tasks
likes.summary: Experiential Learning (EL), developed by Microsoft Research and collaborators, introduces an "LLM-as-a-Coach" framework that transforms rich textual feedback into high-bandwidth learning signals for post-training language models on non-verifiable, open-ended tasks. This method consistently outperformed traditional reinforcement learning, demonstrating improved generalization and reduced reward hacking on various open-ended benchmarks.

likes.title: Intelligence from Learnable Novelty
likes.summary: Researchers at Tufts University and Harvard University propose 'learnable novelty' as a unifying principle for intelligence, and introduce a differentiable estimator for it. This objective successfully drives complex dynamics in cellular automata, enables unsupervised representation learning for MNIST with 0.89 accuracy, and provides a robust intrinsic reward for reinforcement learning agents across various tasks.

likes.title: Measuring Reward-Seeking via Contrastive Belief Updates
likes.summary: Researchers from Apollo Research and OpenAI developed Contrastive Synthetic Document Finetuning (SDF) to quantitatively measure 'reward-seeking' in large language models. The method demonstrated that RL-trained models increasingly prioritize perceived grader preferences, even overriding explicit instructions in some cases, and that models known for 'reward-hacking' exhibited amplified reward-seeking tendencies.

likes.title: Exploration Matters for Escaping the Blur Trap in 3D Gaussian Splatting
likes.summary: Researchers from Hunan University and Nanyang Technological University identified the "Blur Trap" in 3D Gaussian Splatting, a persistent blur caused by biased gradient optimization, and introduced two minimal exploration operators—Random Seeding and Random Splitting—that significantly enhance scene detail and fidelity across diverse datasets.

likes.title: ABot-World-0: Infinite Interactive World Rollout on a Single Desktop GPU
likes.summary: The ABot-World Team at Alibaba Group's AMAP CV Lab developed ABot-World-0, an action-conditioned video world model capable of generating interactive, persistent virtual worlds. It achieves real-time rollout at up to 16 frames per second (FPS) at 720P resolution with 1.2 seconds of action-to-first-frame latency, running on a single desktop GPU with less than 19.3 GiB VRAM.

likes.summary: The researchers developed PATCH POLICY, an efficient, modular Transformer-based policy that directly utilizes dense visual representations from frozen, pre-trained Vision Transformers. This approach achieves superior performance in precise robot manipulation tasks with significantly reduced computational cost and faster inference compared to large Vision-Language-Action models.

likes.title: MoGe-3: Fine-Detail Monocular Geometry Estimation with Self-Guided Sparse Volumetric Refinement
likes.summary: Researchers from Tsinghua University and Microsoft Research developed MoGe-3, a monocular geometry estimation model that integrates a Self-Guided Sparse 3D Refiner to produce geometrically undistorted and detail-preserving metric-scale point maps. The method shows improved accuracy in fine structures and maintains competitive global performance across various benchmarks.

likes.summary: Microsoft Mage Team developed Mage-Flow, a 4B-parameter foundation model that achieves competitive high-resolution image generation and instruction-based editing performance against much larger open-source models, demonstrating significant efficiency with 0.59s for 1024x1024 image generation on an NVIDIA A100 GPU and a 2.48x training speedup through system co-design.

likes.title: RynnBrain 1.1: Towards More Capable and Generalizable Embodied Foundation Model
likes.summary: RynnBrain 1.1, an upgraded family of embodied foundation models from DAMO Academy, Alibaba Group, and Hupan Lab, enhances physical world understanding and generalizability for robot control. It achieves precise 3D grounding and contact point prediction capabilities, leading to significantly improved real-robot manipulation performance across diverse platforms compared to previous models.

likes.title: Agentic Real2Sim: Physics-based World Modeling with Vision-Language Agents
likes.summary: Researchers developed Agentic Real2Sim, a framework for converting real-world robotic interaction recordings into simulatable episodic digital twins. It integrates vision-language agents to orchestrate visual processing, physical parameter inference, and scene preparation, achieving multi-VLM support and demonstrating similar replay success rates with open-weight models at significantly lower computational costs.

likes.title: Automated Discovery Has No Universally Superior Harness
likes.summary: Research at UC Berkeley and MIT demonstrated that no single fixed harness consistently outperforms others in LLM-guided discovery systems across various models and problems. Instead, adaptive allocation strategies that prune less promising runs based on early progress consistently achieved higher average scores, ranging from 84.87% to 85.75%, surpassing non-adaptive baselines.
